title: Pilot VMFA FRS F-35B Qualified (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
12.     MOS 7518, Pilot VMFA FRS F-35B Qualified (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC
AVN

    a. Summary. VMFA Pilots operate network enabled and digitally
interoperable fighter-attack aircraft to provide aviation support across the
full spectrum of combat operations.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Security requirement:     top secret security clearance eligibility.

        (2) Must complete the Centrifuge-Based Flight Environment Trainer
Course (A17KZA1).

        (3) Must meet the requirements of reference (ah) and the USN Manual
of the Medical Department.

        (4) Must complete the Aircrew Refresher NASTP Training Class 3
Aircraft Course (M04P2E7, M17P2E3, N02P2E4, N04P2E5, N06P2E3, N23P2E4,
N26P2E3, N37P2E1).

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Must complete either of the following courses:




                                           1-280                        Enclosure (1)
 1143                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



            (a) The F-35 Category I Course (M16F3F1) MCAS Beaufort, SC;
(M17F3FC) MCAS Miramar, CA; or (N04F3M6) NAS Lemoore, CA; or a USAF CAT I
equivalent course is required for category I students.

            (b) The F-35 Category II Course (M16F351) MCAS Beaufort, SC;
(M17F35C) MCAS Miramar, CA; or (N04F3N6, CAT II-A) (N04F3P6, CAT II-B)
(N04F3Q6, CAT II-C) NAS Lemoore, CA; or a USAF CAT II equivalent is required
for CAT II students.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Provides five of six functions of Marine Aviation in all
weather, day/night conditions to include offensive air support, anti-air
warfare, electronic warfare, assault support and reconnaissance.

        (2) Provides air defense during all weather conditions, day and
night, by coordinating with airborne and/or ground control intercept units to
intercept and destroy attacking enemy aircraft and missiles.

            (3) Operates from naval shipping, expeditionary fields, and/or land
bases.

            (4) Commands or assists in commanding an aviation unit.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
